dimensions.reasons: The Group B hero render clearly reconstructs the intended recycling/crushing line: a lime high-level hopper structure, separate left control cabinet, front crusher/compression unit with drive motor, white/green inclined conveyor, overhead curved duct, safety guard, and studio backdrop. The overall silhouette and product-render presentation closely follow the reference while incorporating a gray transition chute at the conveyor discharge.
issues: The upper tower is more enclosed and box-like than the reference's visibly braced, open steel frame.
The submission replaces the reference's GREENMAX/INTCO branding with ECOPRESS text.
Several lower crusher/processing housings are simplified into smooth rectangular cabinets, making the reconstructed machine less mechanically specific than the reference.

dimensions.reasons: Visible geometry in Group A wide_high, wide_right, and detail_controls is consistently supported: the tall assembly stands on four steel legs with base plates, the conveyor has a triangulated white support frame and multiple casters, and the foreground crusher cabinet is grounded on small wheels. The motor, mesh guard, duct, hopper, and transition assembly appear attached rather than floating.
issues: The gray transition-chute/bracket assembly beneath the conveyor head is visually busy and its final connection into the green hopper is somewhat hard to read.
Some of the wheeled lower equipment looks more mobile/lightweight than a heavy industrial crusher body.

dimensions.reasons: The object silhouettes are independently recognizable as industrial equipment rather than generic blobs: Group B and Group A cam_submitted show the tall hopper, teal feed tray, cylindrical motor, guarded drive, control console, and conveyor. The lime-yellow structure, deep green accents, teal belt, white conveyor rails, and black mechanical details closely match the target palette.
issues: The solid flat white roof and largely closed tower panels depart from the more open, diagonally braced upper architecture in the reference.
Some lower lime-green housings remain visually plain and box-like, with limited functional differentiation beyond a vent grille and inspection windows.

dimensions.reasons: The designated Group B hero is a clean, coherent product-style render with soft floor shadows, crisp belt cleats, readable control hardware, and no obvious geometry breakage. Mechanical additions such as roller hubs, a ribbed motor coupling, mesh guard, and fastener-like elements improve believability.
issues: The render is noticeably overbright in white and pale lime regions, reducing contrast around the tower roof, white conveyor frame, and panel seams.
Many painted surfaces look uniformly smooth and CG-like rather than like slightly varied industrial coated metal.
Small equipment details and labels are less convincing at close inspection than the larger forms.

dimensions.reasons: The spatial organization shown in Group B hero and Group A wide_high closely follows the target: the freestanding control cabinet sits left of the processing line, the elevated hopper structure is back/left, the crusher/feed section is in front of it, and the conveyor occupies the right side running up into the feed area. The added gray transition funnel visibly bridges the conveyor head toward the hopper/main-machine inlet.
issues: The conveyor still reads as fairly steep in the hero view rather than as a clearly, substantially relaxed incline.
The foreground green feed tray is more prominent and separated from the tall structure than the reference hopper integration.

dimensions.reasons: The major equipment proportions are generally sensible: the tower is tallest, the conveyor is long and floor-supported, the control cabinet is human-scale relative to the machine, and casters/motor dimensions read plausibly. The complete line fits coherently within the Group B studio view.
issues: The upper tower appears somewhat shorter and more compact relative to the lower processing equipment than in the reference.
The front wheeled crusher cabinet/feed hopper appears somewhat oversized and more self-contained relative to the high hopper frame.
The separate control cabinet is slightly more isolated from the main installation than in the reference composition.

dimensions.reasons: The Group B final has the requested clean light-gray studio setting, broad soft illumination, and grounded shadows. Material categories are distinguishable: the cabinet is gray metal, the main structure is painted lime metal, the conveyor has white structural rails and a teal rubber-like cleated belt, and motors/rollers are dark mechanical materials. Group A detail_conveyor clearly shows raised white chevrons on the belt.
issues: The requested brushed stainless texture on the control cabinet is only weakly evident; it reads mostly as smooth uniform gray metal.
The lime structural paint is relatively glossy and plasticky instead of clearly matte painted steel.
Bright white surfaces are partially washed out, especially on the roof and conveyor framework.

dimensions.reasons: All key requested visible objects are present in the submitted views: a separate populated control cabinet, elevated branded hopper/tower, curved white duct, central feed/crusher assembly, black cylindrical drive motor, mesh safety guard, wheeled conveyor with white frame and green chevron belt, and an added gray transfer hopper/chute. Group A detail_controls and detail_conveyor substantiate the small safety and belt features that are easy to lose in the wide shot.
issues: The reference's prominent open-frame bracing and more exposed internal lower-machine/fan structure are reduced or obscured.
The lower conveyor intake is less broadly flared and detailed than the reference intake tray.
Some important lower housings are present but their processing roles are not as legible as in the reference.

criteria.criterion: The reconstruction forms a complete equipment line with the specified regional organization and reference-like relative scale hierarchy.
The left operating station combines the required cabinet identity, visible controls, and modified brushed-stainless finish.
The rear hopper retains its elevated support, salient reference construction, upper branding, and attached curved guide pipe.
The central processing assembly combines a recognizable shredding-and-compaction body, readable processing-region cues, and a plausibly mounted cylindrical drive motor.
The right conveyor combines the specified frame, patterned belt, attached casters, and gentler modified incline.
The added transition hopper physically and legibly connects the conveyor discharge to the main-machine inlet.
The complete equipment line uses the required palette and a distinguishable matte painted-frame material system.
The native scene and final render implement deliberate three-point soft product lighting.
The designated final render combines the specified studio background and camera composition with unobstructed educational readability and a clean product-grade finish.
criteria.evidence: The designated final render, recycling_crusher_hero_3840x2880.png, presents the complete equipment line in a clean pale gray-white studio setting from an elevated three-quarter angle. The separate left control cabinet has clearly visible rows of indicators, buttons, labels, and an emergency stop; the white-framed green cleated conveyor visibly rises into the gray transition chute and open green hopper; and both the prominent dark cylindrical drive and the white wire safety guard are readable. Major machine frames, hopper, cabinet, conveyor support, and casters are visible without clutter or material occlusion, with coherent soft shadows and finished product-render shading.

criteria.criterion: A genuine high-resolution completed author render is delivered as an openable image.
The delivered Blender project is openable, editable, and suitable for later annotation and alternate camera views.

notes: This is a clearly recognizable, largely complete reconstruction of the industrial recycling line, with especially strong component coverage, conveyor detailing, supports, and clean product-shot composition in the Group B hero render. The main limitations are a more generic enclosed tower and simplified crusher body, a conveyor that does not read as markedly flatter, weakly brushed/matte material treatment, and overbright low-contrast lighting. The blank Group A wide_front and wide_back evaluator views do not outweigh the clearly visible final hero image and other successful geometry views.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
